subject: science
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF
note: Replaces the earlier 12-chapter NCERT Class 9 Science book. Hindi edition: Anveshan.

chapters.title: Exploration: Entering the World of Secondary Science

topics.title: Models and simplification in science
outcomes: Learner can explain why scientists build simplified models and decide which details can be ignored for a given question
misconceptions: Thinks a model is wrong because it leaves out details
Thinks the branches of science are unrelated
hooks: A cricket ball treated as a single point; Meghnad Saha linking star colour to temperature

topics.title: Mathematics, symbols and standard units
outcomes: Learner can use symbols, equations and SI units consistently and explain why standard units matter
misconceptions: Believes the unit is optional once you have the number
hooks: The passenger jet that ran short of fuel because of a unit mix-up; a sabziwala’s pan balance and standard weights

topics.title: Laws, theories and hypotheses
outcomes: Learner can distinguish the everyday and scientific meanings of words like hypothesis, law and theory
misconceptions: Thinks a scientific theory is just a guess
hooks: Why conservation of energy is trusted everywhere

chapters.title: Cell: The Building Block of Life

topics.title: Structure of a cell
outcomes: Learner can describe the cell membrane, cell wall, nucleus and organelles and their functions
misconceptions: Believes cells are flat two-dimensional shapes
Thinks only plant cells have a nucleus
hooks: Why raisins swell in water (osmosis)

topics.title: Cell division
outcomes: Learner can distinguish mitosis and meiosis and their roles in growth and reproduction
misconceptions: Thinks cells grow bigger forever instead of dividing
hooks: How a cut on your finger heals

topics.title: Cell theory
outcomes: Learner can state the cell theory and how it developed from evidence
misconceptions: Believes cells can arise from non-living matter
hooks: Hooke’s cork cells; modern microscopes

topics.title: Plant tissues
outcomes: Learner can describe meristematic and permanent tissues and how plants grow
misconceptions: Thinks plants grow from all parts equally
hooks: Why grass grows back after mowing

topics.title: Animal tissues
outcomes: Learner can identify epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissues and their functions
misconceptions: Believes blood is not a tissue
hooks: Why a sprain hurts and takes time to heal

topics.title: The musculoskeletal system and joints
outcomes: Learner can explain how bones, muscles and joints (ball-and-socket, hinge, pivot) work together in movement
misconceptions: Thinks muscles can push as well as pull
hooks: Bowling action in cricket; turning your neck

topics.title: Position, distance and displacement
outcomes: Learner can distinguish distance and displacement using a reference point
misconceptions: Believes displacement is always equal to distance
hooks: A lap of the school track: distance 400 m, displacement zero

topics.title: Speed, velocity and acceleration
outcomes: Learner can calculate average speed, velocity and acceleration
misconceptions: Thinks acceleration only means speeding up
Believes an object with zero velocity cannot be accelerating
hooks: A cricket ball thrown straight up at the top

topics.title: Position-time and velocity-time graphs
outcomes: Learner can draw and interpret x-t and v-t graphs, including area and slope
misconceptions: Reads a position-time graph as a picture of the path
hooks: Graph the auto ride to school

topics.title: Equations of motion and circular motion
outcomes: Learner can use kinematic equations for uniform acceleration and describe uniform circular motion
misconceptions: Thinks uniform circular motion has no acceleration
hooks: Braking distance of a bus; a stone in a sling

topics.title: Solutions and concentration
outcomes: Learner can express concentration of a solution and explain solubility
misconceptions: Thinks a concentrated solution is the same as a saturated one
hooks: ORS solution: right amount of salt and sugar

topics.title: Separating homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures
outcomes: Learner can choose and explain methods like crystallisation, separating funnel, sublimation and chromatography
misconceptions: Believes evaporation and crystallisation give the same purity
hooks: Camphor sublimation; separating oil and water

topics.title: Suspensions, colloids and the Tyndall effect
outcomes: Learner can distinguish solutions, suspensions and colloids and explain the Tyndall effect
misconceptions: Thinks milk is a solution
hooks: Sunbeams through a dusty room; car headlights in fog

topics.title: Balanced and unbalanced forces, friction
outcomes: Learner can find the net force on an object and relate it to change in motion, including friction
misconceptions: Believes constant velocity needs a constant net force
hooks: Tug of war on sports day

topics.title: Newton’s first and second laws
outcomes: Learner can explain inertia and use F = ma
misconceptions: Thinks heavier objects fall faster in the absence of air
Believes a force is "used up" as an object moves
hooks: Passengers jerk forward when a bus brakes

topics.title: Newton’s third law and systems
outcomes: Learner can identify action-reaction pairs and explain why they do not cancel
misconceptions: Thinks action and reaction act on the same object and cancel
hooks: Recoil of a gun; jumping off a boat

topics.title: Work done by a force
outcomes: Learner can calculate work done and identify positive, negative and zero work
misconceptions: Believes holding a heavy bag still is doing work in the physics sense
hooks: Coolie carrying luggage on a flat platform

topics.title: Kinetic and potential energy, conservation
outcomes: Learner can calculate kinetic and potential energy and apply conservation of mechanical energy
misconceptions: Thinks energy is used up and disappears
hooks: A swing at its highest and lowest points

topics.title: Power
outcomes: Learner can calculate power and compare machines and people doing the same work
misconceptions: Confuses power with energy or force
hooks: Climbing stairs quickly vs slowly

topics.title: Simple machines
outcomes: Learner can explain how levers, pulleys and inclined planes make work easier
misconceptions: Believes machines reduce the work done
hooks: A well pulley; ramp to load a truck

topics.title: History of atomic models
outcomes: Learner can trace atomic ideas from Kanada’s parmanu to Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford and Bohr and the evidence for each
misconceptions: Thinks atoms can be seen with an ordinary microscope
Believes electrons orbit the nucleus exactly like planets
hooks: Rutherford’s gold foil experiment as a "throw marbles at a hidden shape" game

topics.title: Subatomic particles, atomic number and mass number
outcomes: Learner can determine numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons from atomic and mass numbers
misconceptions: Thinks the mass number counts electrons
hooks: Periodic table posters in the lab

topics.title: Electron distribution and valency
outcomes: Learner can write electron distributions for the first 20 elements and find valency
misconceptions: Believes valency is always equal to the number of outer electrons
hooks: Why neon signs glow but neon does not react

topics.title: Isotopes
outcomes: Learner can explain isotopes and give examples of their uses
misconceptions: Thinks isotopes are different elements
hooks: Cobalt-60 in cancer treatment; carbon dating

topics.title: Laws of chemical combination
outcomes: Learner can state and verify the laws of conservation of mass and constant proportions
misconceptions: Believes mass is lost when something burns
hooks: Weigh a sealed bottle of vinegar and baking soda

topics.title: Ionic and covalent bonding
outcomes: Learner can explain bond formation by electron transfer and sharing and compare properties of ionic and covalent compounds
misconceptions: Thinks ionic compounds conduct electricity even as solids
hooks: Why salt water conducts but sugar water does not

topics.title: Chemical formulae and molecular mass
outcomes: Learner can write formulae using valency and calculate molecular and formula unit masses
misconceptions: Writes NaCl2 by not balancing valencies
hooks: Formula of the antacid in your medicine cabinet

topics.title: Production and propagation of sound
outcomes: Learner can explain that sound is produced by vibration and needs a medium, travelling as longitudinal waves
misconceptions: Believes sound can travel through a vacuum
Thinks air particles travel from the source to the ear
hooks: Tabla skin vibrating; astronauts using radios on the Moon

topics.title: Frequency, amplitude, speed and hearing
outcomes: Learner can relate frequency to pitch and amplitude to loudness and compare speed of sound in media
misconceptions: Thinks louder sounds have a higher pitch
hooks: The veena’s thick and thin strings

topics.title: Reflection of sound: echo, reverberation, echolocation
outcomes: Learner can explain echoes, reverberation and uses of ultrasound and echolocation
misconceptions: Believes an echo can be heard in any room
hooks: Gol Gumbaz whispering gallery; bats and SONAR

topics.title: Asexual reproduction and vegetative propagation
outcomes: Learner can describe modes of asexual reproduction and vegetative propagation and their uses in agriculture
misconceptions: Thinks offspring from asexual reproduction differ from the parent like siblings do
hooks: Sugarcane grown from stem pieces; potato eyes

topics.title: Sexual reproduction in flowering plants
outcomes: Learner can explain pollination, fertilisation and seed formation and why meiosis creates variation
misconceptions: Believes all flowers can produce fruit without pollination
hooks: Bees on a mango tree in bloom

topics.title: Human reproduction and reproductive health
outcomes: Learner can describe human reproductive maturity, organs and pregnancy in outline, and ways to stay healthy and safe
misconceptions: Thinks reproductive health is not a topic for students to understand
hooks: Why adolescent health clinics (AFHCs) exist

chapters.title: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

topics.title: India’s biodiversity
outcomes: Learner can explain why India is a biodiversity hotspot and why diversity matters
misconceptions: Thinks biodiversity means only large animals
hooks: Western Ghats frogs; Northeast orchids

topics.title: Classification and the five kingdoms
outcomes: Learner can classify organisms into five kingdoms using cell type, body organisation and nutrition
misconceptions: Believes fungi are plants
Thinks whales are fish and bats are birds
hooks: Mushrooms on a rotting log

topics.title: Hierarchy, binomial names and fossils
outcomes: Learner can use the hierarchy of classification and binomial names and explain fossils as evidence of past life
misconceptions: Thinks common names are as precise as scientific names
hooks: Panthera tigris; dinosaur fossils of Balasinor, Gujarat

chapters.title: Earth as a System: Energy, Matter, and Life

topics.title: Uneven heating of the Earth
outcomes: Learner can explain how latitude, Earth’s shape and the atmosphere cause uneven heating
misconceptions: Believes it is hotter near the equator because it is closer to the Sun
hooks: Chennai vs Srinagar temperatures in January

topics.title: Winds and ocean currents
outcomes: Learner can explain local and planetary winds and ocean currents as results of uneven heating
misconceptions: Thinks ocean currents are caused only by tides
hooks: The monsoon and Indian Ocean currents

topics.title: Biogeochemical cycles
outcomes: Learner can describe the water, carbon, nitrogen and oxygen cycles
misconceptions: Thinks the atoms in our bodies are destroyed when we die
hooks: Root nodules on pulses fixing nitrogen

topics.title: Human impact on Earth’s processes
outcomes: Learner can analyse how human activity disrupts natural cycles and suggest responses
misconceptions: Believes climate and weather are the same thing
hooks: Stubble burning and winter smog in north India
